plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered flower heads in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It thrives in the shortening days of fall and is widely grown in gardens and as cut flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia, especially China and Japan
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants, meaning they set buds when nights grow longer. The flower is the national flower of Japan's Imperial seal tradition and is celebrated at the annual Festival of Happiness.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular subtropical tree that becomes covered in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before its fern-like leaves fully emerge. Entire streets turn purple when it blooms, and the fallen flowers carpet the ground.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Grafton, Sydney), Argentina, and New Zealand's northern regions
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, and a local superstition in Australia says that if a jacaranda flower falls on your head, you'll pass your exams.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust North American wildflower with clusters of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It is one of the last major nectar sources for migrating monarch butterflies and other pollinators late in the season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to late autumn (August to October, lingering into early November in mild areas)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America in meadows, roadsides, and wet prairies
plants.funFact: The flower heads close at night and on cloudy days, and the plant's late bloom makes it a critical fuel stop for monarch butterflies on their migration to Mexico.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub producing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl of pointed pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It thrives in nutrient-poor, fire-prone fynbos habitats.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering in spring (September to November)
plants.location: Southwestern and southern coastal regions of South Africa, including the Cape Floral Region
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and the genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape, reflecting the great diversity of protea forms.
